bounds: Six outcomes cover one morning summary with a valid model response, blank text, absent model, rejected generation, rejected report write, or an unsupported explicit current-day declaration. Date validation covers English named dates, ISO dates and US numeric dates in report-date declarations; ordinary source event dates remain allowed. The implementation check uses the real CheckinService and PGlite with controlled model and storage outcomes. Collector accuracy, provider output quality, scheduling, delivery and cancellation at the scheduler boundary remain separate checks. Safety is unconditional. Completion assumes collection, model resolution and storage resolution each eventually return. Calendar change projection covers one owner-scoped candidate row, Google or local origin, malformed metadata, absent/old/recent/invalid provider clock classes, two cache-clock classes and today membership. Provider clock priority is updatedAt, updated, then createdAt. Invalid selected metadata stays unknown and reports partial coverage. Projection has one deterministic enabled step, so no fairness assumption is needed. Existing database tests cover date parsing, isolation, unchanged storage and filtering before the forty-item window. The model does not prove database candidate completeness, arbitrary dates or provider synchronization.
